title: Studying data science in Germany
description: Which universities teach data science in English, what the programmes cost, what they require and where graduates end up working.
html:
Data science has become one of the most requested subjects among international applicants to German universities, and for good reason: the programmes are strong, most are taught in English, tuition at public universities is close to zero and employers are hiring. This guide covers the essentials.

Why Germany for data science

German universities combine solid mathematics and computer science foundations with applied work in industry, and the country's manufacturing, automotive, pharmaceutical and financial sectors generate real demand for people who can work with data. Graduates get an 18-month job-seeker permit after finishing, which is more than most countries offer.

The degrees on offer

At bachelor's level, data science usually appears as a specialisation within computer science or as a stand-alone programme at universities of applied sciences. The English-taught choice is much wider at master's level, where programmes range from statistically oriented to engineering-heavy. Look closely at the curriculum: a programme called data science can lean towards machine learning, business analytics or statistics, and the right one depends on your background.

Where to study

The large technical universities in Munich, Aachen, Berlin, Darmstadt and Karlsruhe all offer English-taught master's programmes with a data science focus and have the strongest links to industry. Universities in Hamburg, Tübingen and Saarbrücken are known for machine learning research. Several universities of applied sciences offer more practice-oriented programmes with compulsory industry semesters, which suit students who want to work rather than pursue a PhD.

What you need to apply

A bachelor's degree with a substantial share of mathematics, statistics and programming is the usual requirement, often with a minimum grade. English at IELTS 6.5 or equivalent is standard. Some programmes ask for a GRE score, a letter of motivation and, increasingly, a short description of a project you have worked on. Deadlines for the winter semester tend to fall between January and May.

Careers

Graduates work as data scientists, machine learning engineers and analysts at car makers, industrial groups, banks, insurers, e-commerce companies and consultancies. Starting salaries for master's graduates typically sit between €50,000 and €65,000, higher in Munich and Frankfurt. German helps in many companies, but a large share of data teams work in English.

Practical preparation

Start the financial side early. The student visa requires proof of about €11,904 in a Blocked Account and valid health insurance, and both should be in place before your embassy appointment. Setting them up together, before you have the admission letter in hand, is the simplest way to avoid a delay at the end of the process.
